newsitem.title: USA: Polaroid off after guiding analysts lower.
newsitem.headline: Polaroid off after guiding analysts lower.

text.p: Polaroid Corp shares fell on Wednesday after management lowered its estimates for 1996 operating earnings, an analyst said.

Eugene Glazer, an analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds, said company executives told analysts in a conference telephone call late on Tuesday they were lowering projected operating earnings for the year to about $200 million from $225 million.

Polaroid's stock was off 7/8 to 43-1/8 in late morning trade. Glazer said the new estimate meant fourth-quarter earnings per share (EPS) could fall to about $0.85 from a First Call consensus estimate of $1.13.
The news on Tuesday came just hours after the company reported third-quarter earnings of $0.74, up from $0.51 in 1995, and above the First Call consensus of $0.67.
"They had good earnings and bad guidance," Glazer said. A company spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
Polaroid reported a $157.8 million loss from operations in 1995.
Polaroid said on Tuesday it was addressing its sales drop in Russia, which contributed to the company's third-quarter decline in worldwide sales.
